questions.question: Explain how the king's interaction with the hermit and the wounded man leads to the answers to his three questions.
questions.solution_html:
• Explain how the king's interaction with the hermit and the wounded man leads to the answers to
  • his three questions.
  • Ans: The king approached a hermit -He was sowing the seeds and digging - even though the king
  • asked for the answers the hermit ignored him.-The king offered his help-At that time a bearded man
  • was running towards them- He was a wounded man with bleeding in the stomach. The king cleaned
  • his wound and dressed him-Then they took him inside the house-Later they knew that the man was
  • the one who came to take revenge on the king as he had killed his brother and taken his property-
  • But king’s bodyguards who knew this wounded him- Now he regretted and apologized- The king was
  • pleased to turn his enemy into a friend- Thus the wounded man became the most important man.-
  • Nursing the wounded man was the most important work to do- To do good for others as we are sent
  • for this noble cause is the greatest job-The most important time is the present time as we have tḥe
  • power to act-Thus the king got happy with the hermit’s answers for the three questions.

questions.question: What does Kipling mean by "If you can fill the unforgiving minute / With sixty seconds' worth of distance run"? / [CO5]
questions.solution_html:
• Use every moment of life to the fullest. The “unforgiving minute” suggests time never stops
  • or returns. To fill it with “sixty seconds’ worth of distance run” = make every second
  • meaningful through action [U] / [CO5]

questions.question: Explain how Foreman becomes successful in his new business venture.
questions.solution_html:
• Explain how Foreman becomes successful in his new business venture.
  • Ans: Foreman is really unhappy and distressed when he exits the church- He moves slowly along the
  • lengthy road, carefully considering what he should do next- He has a pitiful sum of money, but it is
  • not enough to support his family's needs without working- He doesn't smoke, but he likes a cigarette
  • when he's upset or worn out- He wants to smoke, which would make him feel better- In the lengthy
  • street, he is unable to locate a tobacco store-
  • He thinks that it sounds odd- He believes that a tobacco business would be successful in such a
  • location- He follows through with his plan on the following day- He launches his tobacco company by
  • renting a suitable store- After turning a profit, he opens ten branches around London in ten years-
  • He develops into a successful businessman

questions.question: Discuss the moral lessons Tolstoy aims to convey through the story "The Three Questions."
questions.solution_html:
• Discuss the moral lessons Tolstoy aims to convey through the story "The Three Questions."
  • Ans: about a king seeking answers to three questions: What is the right time to do something? Who
  • is the most important person to listen to? What is the most important thing to do? - The king sets
  • out on a journey to find the answers and meets three different people along the way- Each person
  • provides him with a different answer to his questions, but he is not satisfied- In the end, through the
  • interaction with hermit and wounded man the king learns that the most important time is the
  • present moment, the most important person is the one you are with, and the most important action
  • is to do good for others –moral : focus on the present and not worry about the past or future- Three
  • Questions serves as a template for a meaningful life.

questions.question: How does Rudyard Kipling's poem "If—" project the English ideal of manhood? / [CO5]
questions.solution_html:
• Kipling projects manhood not through physical strength or domination but through
  • character, self-control, endurance, integrity, and balanced judgment. These qualities reflect
  • the English Victorian ideal of the gentleman, making the poem a moral blueprint for the
  • ideal citizen of the British Empire [An] / [CO 5]
